title: Planar Symmetric Pattern Generation
claim: One framework generates visually rich, continuous patterns that exactly satisfy every one of a full family of symmetry groups.
layout: 17 panels in 6x3 grid, row-major, legend of symmetry operations bottom-right
description: A tall grid of 17 square pattern samples, three per row, one for each planar (wallpaper) symmetry group: p1, p2, pm, pg, cm, p2mm, p2mg, p2gg, c2mm, p4, p4mm, p4gm, p3, p3m1, p31m, p6, p6mm. The group name is a bold label above each panel. Every panel shows a stained-glass mosaic texture in pale blues, greens, greys and a few warm accents. Overlaid black lines mark the symmetry operations: thin solid lines for translation, thick solid lines for mirrors, dashed lines for glide reflections. Small black ovals, triangles, diamonds and hexagons mark 2-, 3-, 4- and 6-fold rotation centers. The patterns grow denser and more intricate going down the grid. The last row has an empty slot that holds the legend titled 'Symmetric Operation'. The eye goes first to the grid of dense, kaleidoscopic textures.
caption: Generated images for the 17 planar groups using the prompt stained-glass mosaic fragments... Annotated symmetry transformations demonstrate that our patterns exhibit perceptual preservation of the target symmetries.
abstract: Generating objects with specific symmetries is essential in various real-world scenarios. However, adapting existing 2D continuous representations to enforce planar group symmetry remains a challenge, as the transformation of non-reflective group elements may disrupt continuity. To overcome this limitation, we propose a symmetrization framework for arbitrary planar groups. Our method transforms any 2D continuous representation into a symmetric one while preserving continuity. We provide the mathematical formulation of this representation, demonstrate its approximation capability for symmetric functions, and detail the construction methodology. We validate our approach through three visual design tasks (pattern design, paper-cutting design and stylized topology design) and one material design task. Experiments confirm that our representation enables effective symmetry control and demonstrate its broader applicability.
